source.title_or_context: **Table 14 Core components of cardiac rehabilitation in patients with chronic kidney disease.**

table_assessment.assessment_notes: Exact review confirms CKD risk assessment, tailored exercise, dialysis/transplant precautions, education, diet, lipid, and BP instructions. Medication/supplement recommendations coexist with non-drug instructions, and two management/adaptation actions are underspecified.

entities.surface_form: Risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, family history of kidney disease) and symptoms of CKD (e.g. proteinuria)
KDIGO 2012 categories (low, moderate, high, very-high risk, based on albuminuria A1–A3, and glomerular filtration rate G1 to G5)

normative_assertions.notes: Risk factors/symptoms and KDIGO-category risk stratification should be assessed.

text_units.verbatim_text: • Risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, family history of kidney disease) and symptoms of CKD (e.g. proteinuria) • Risk stratification according to the KDIGO 2012 categories (low, moderate, high, very-high risk, based on albuminuria A1–A3, and glomerular filtration rate G1 to G5) should be performed

entities.surface_form: combination of endurance and resistance exercise (especially lower body exercise) and activities to develop flexibility, coordination and body awareness
very high risk CKD and haemodialysis patients
exercises (gymnastics and resistance exercises) which include pressing on the arms and/or holding the arms in head up position
vulnerability of the kidney transplant in the fossa iliaca directly under the abdominal wall, the reduced perfusion of the transplant and adverse effects of the immunosuppressive therapy
exercises performed in face down position and extreme stretching exercises for the upper part of the body

normative_assertions.notes: The programme should include the listed exercise/activity domains.
Exercise training should be tailored to physical capacity and CKD severity.
For low-to-high CKD risk, the programme should be deduced from heart disease.
The OCR says ET may have to be 'adopted'; the intended adaptation/adoption operation is uncertain.
Protect the puncture area with dressing during exercise.
Haemodialysis patients should not wear wrist devices.
Do not measure BP on the shunt-arm side.
HR may be measured on the shunt-arm side.
Avoid arm-pressing/head-up-position exercises.
Schedule ET between haemodialysis treatments.
Consider transplant vulnerability, perfusion, and immunosuppressive adverse effects.
Avoid face-down and extreme upper-body stretching exercises after kidney transplantation.

text_units.verbatim_text: The programme should include a combination of endurance and resistance exercise (especially lower body exercise) and activities to develop flexibility, coordination and body awareness. See Gollie et al. 150 for other programme details For a given patient, ET should depend on the baseline level of physical capacity and the CKD severity. In low to high risk patients, the CKD usually does not affect the exercise programme, which should be deduced by the heart disease. In very high risk CKD and haemodialysis patients ET may have to be adopted Special advice for haemodialysis patients: • To avoid injury of the arteriovenous fistula and pain in the shunt-arm: the puncture-area should be protected with dressing while exercising • Patients should not wear wristwatches or wristbands • BP should not be measured on the shunt-arm side • HR can more easily be measured on the shunt-arm side • Avoid exercises (gymnastics and resistance exercises) which include pressing on the arms and/or holding the arms in head up position • ET should be performed on the day between haemodialysis treatments Special advice for patients after kidney transplantation • Consider the vulnerability of the kidney transplant in the fossa iliaca directly under the abdominal wall, the reduced perfusion of the transplant and adverse effects of the immunosuppressive therapy • Avoid exercises performed in face down position and extreme stretching exercises for the upper part of the body

normative_assertions.notes: The educational programme covers CKD and cardiac-disease self-management.

text_units.verbatim_text: Self-management of CKD and cardiac disease

entities.surface_form: patients with higher stage of the CKD
intake of foods rich in phosphate (e.g. milk products, eggs and meat)
intake of food rich in potassium (e.g. fresh fruits, nuts, fruit juice)
vitamin D analogue (calcitol, afacitol or paracitol)

normative_assertions.notes: Consider hyperphosphataemia and hypocalcaemia in higher-stage CKD.
Reduce phosphate-rich food intake.
Calcium supplementation is recommended.
Reduce potassium-rich food intake.
Consider a vitamin D analogue in stage V CKD.
Consider water-soluble vitamin supplementation.

text_units.verbatim_text: • In patients with higher stage of the CKD hyper-phosphataemia and hypocalcaemia have to be considered and the intake of foods rich in phosphate (e.g. milk products, eggs and meat) should be reduced, whereas calcium supplementation is recommended • The intake of food rich in potassium (e.g. fresh fruits, nuts, fruit juice) should be reduced • The supplementation of a vitamin D analogue (calcitol, afacitol or paracitol) should be considered in stage V CKD; supplementation of water soluble vitamins should be considered

entities.surface_form: high (stage 3 CKD) or very-high risk (stage 4–5 CKD or on dialysis) of CVD

normative_assertions.notes: Management is explicitly recommended but underspecified in the isolated row.

text_units.verbatim_text: Patients with CKD are considered to be at high (stage 3 CKD) or very-high risk (stage 4–5 CKD or on dialysis) of CVD, and should be managed accordingly

normative_assertions.notes: Arterial hypertension should be detected.
Hypertension should be treated to CKD-specific targets; the treatment modality is unspecified.
source_trigger_texts: should properly be detected and treated

text_units.verbatim_text: Arterial hypertension as the leading risk factor should properly be detected and treated, according to CKD-specific targets
